title: Beef Tallow vs Butter: Which Has More Saturated Fat?

seo.title: Beef Tallow vs Butter: Saturated Fat Compared
seo.meta_description: Butter and beef tallow are both high in saturated fat. Per 100 g, butter is about 51 g saturated fat and tallow is around 50 g, so the practical gap is small.
seo.search_intent: Compare saturated fat, calories, and cooking use in beef tallow and butter.

excerpt: Butter and beef tallow are both concentrated fats and contain similar amounts of saturated fat—roughly half their weight in a 100-gram comparison. Neither offers a major advantage if your goal is to lower saturated fat.
content_html:
Tallow is often presented as a very different cooking fat from butter, but the saturated-fat comparison is surprisingly close. Both are concentrated sources of saturated fat.

Per 100 grams, there is no dramatic winner

USDA composition data put butter at roughly 51 grams of saturated fat per 100 grams and beef tallow around 50 grams, depending on the specific entry. Tallow is nearly pure fat, while butter contains some water and milk solids, so tallow can be slightly more calorie-dense by weight.

At a tablespoon scale, butter provides about 7 grams of saturated fat, with tallow in a similar range. Portion size matters more than a tiny difference between database entries.

The cooking behavior is more different than the nutrition

Butter's water and milk solids affect browning and flavor. Rendered tallow is essentially an anhydrous animal fat with a beefier flavor. They can therefore produce different results even when their saturated-fat totals are close.

For less saturated fat, change categories

Replacing some of either fat with olive, canola, or another unsaturated oil creates a much larger shift in fatty-acid profile. Choose between tallow and butter for culinary reasons, not because one is a low-saturated-fat option.

faq.question: Does tallow have more saturated fat than butter?
faq.answer: They are generally close per 100 grams: butter is around 51 grams and tallow roughly 50 grams, with product variation.

faq.question: Which has more calories?
faq.answer: Tallow can be slightly more calorie-dense because it is nearly pure fat, while butter contains water and milk solids.

faq.question: Which is better for lowering saturated fat?
faq.answer: Neither offers a major advantage. Replacing part of either with an unsaturated oil makes a much bigger difference.
